header: IN THE ISLAMABAD HIGH COURT, ISLAMABAD
PETITIONER BY: Mr. M. Yaqoob Javaid, Advocate
RESPONDENTS BY: Mr. Amir Latif Gill, Advocate
Mr. Saud Gul, DAO Pension-I, CDA
body: AYYAZ SHAUKAT, J:- Through the instant petition under Article 199 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 (the "Constitution"), the petitioner, a retired Audit Officer (BS-18) of the Capital Development Authority ("CDA"), seeks a direction to CDA to issue his pension payment order and to pay the arrears of his pension with effect from 01.04.2024, together with the commuted value of pension, as sanctioned by the Pension Sanctioning Authority. He also prays that the delay be declared illegal and discriminatory, and that markup be allowed on the amounts withheld.

2. The facts, in brief, are that the petitioner was appointed in CDA as Divisional Account (Audit) Officer (BPS-16) in January 2008, after an interview and test, against a post which the offer of appointment described as "regular and pensionable". Before that, he had served Pakistan Telecommunication Company Limited ("PTCL") and had left it under the voluntary separation scheme, commonly called the golden handshake. He retired from CDA as Audit Officer (BS-18) on attaining the age of superannuation with effect from 31.03.2024. The Member Finance of CDA, as the Pension Sanctioning Authority, accorded sanction to his pension. The sanction records a qualifying service of 16 years, 02 months and 24 days, a gross pension of Rs.40,768/- per month and a commuted value of W.P No. 3352 of 2026 2 Rs.2,118,386/-, and directs that payment "may commence w.e.f 01.04.2024". It also certifies that no inquiry is pending against the petitioner and that no recovery is outstanding. No pension payment order was issued. The petitioner approached the Wafaqi Mohtasib, whose Advisor disposed of his complaint on 27.04.2026 under Article 33 of the Establishment of the Office of Wafaqi Mohtasib (Ombudsman) Order, 1983 (the "Order of 1983"). He has thereafter invoked the jurisdiction of this Court.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the inaction of CDA in paying a sanctioned pension violates Articles 4, 9 and 25 of the Constitution. He submits that under regulations 21.01, 21.21 and 21.25(1)(b) of the Capital Development Authority Employees (Service) Regulations, 1992 (the "Regulations"), an employee who retires on superannuation after ten years of qualifying service is entitled to pension, and that the pension had to be paid within one month of retirement, failing which anticipatory pension was payable under regulation 21.01(4). He adds that a colleague of the petitioner, who also came from PTCL, is drawing pension from CDA after thirteen years of service, and that the cause of action is a recurring one. He relies on Nasir Kamal v. Federation of Pakistan (2021 PLC (C.S.) 1226), Muhammad Azram v. National Institute of Health (2015 PLC (C.S.) 537), Chief Commissioner Inland Revenue, Regional Tax Office, Bahawalpur v. Baqa Muhammad Lashari (2024 SCMR 1164), In the matter of: Haji Muhammad Ismail Memon, Advocate (PLD 2007 SC 35) and other judgments.

4. Conversely, learned counsel for CDA contends that the Regulations are non-statutory and the petition is, therefore, not maintainable. He submits that CDA has a grievance committee for its employees, and that the petitioner, having chosen to approach the Wafaqi Mohtasib, cannot invoke another remedy. On merits, he argues that the pension case is "under observation" for three reasons. First, the petitioner's service in CDA is less than the twenty-five years mentioned in regulation 19.02-A. Second, the petitioner availed the golden handshake from PTCL, and as there is no concept of double pension under Article 529 of the Civil Service Regulations, CDA has asked PTCL to verify the benefits paid to him. Third, W.P No. 3352 of 2026 3 inquiries of the Federal Investigation Agency ("FIA") are pending against him. He adds that the petitioner has suppressed material facts.
5. Arguments heard and record perused. On 16.10.2026, learned counsel for CDA sought time to liaise with the department, but no decision of CDA on the pension case has been placed on record.

6. The objection to maintainability must be decided first. It rests on the premise that the Regulations are non-statutory. That premise is incorrect. The Regulations state that they are made "in exercise of powers conferred by section 51 of the Capital Development Authority Ordinance, 1960 (XXIII of 1960), read with section 37 and section 38 thereof". They were notified vide No.CDA/Reg- 12/92 dated 07.03.1992 for publication in the Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary. The Hon’ble Supreme Court has taken the same view of these very Regulations. In Capital Development Authority through Chairman, Islamabad v. Shabir Hussain (2022 SCMR 627), where CDA had challenged a judgment of this Court passed in writ jurisdiction in favour of its employees, the Supreme Court observed: "Consistent with section 51 of the Capital Development Authority Ordinance, 1960, the Authority may make Regulations and publish it in the Official Gazette. ... In exercise of aforesaid powers conferred on the Authority, the Capital Development Authority Employees (Service) Regulations, 1992 were enacted."
7. The Regulations being statutory, the case falls under paragraph 50(i) of Pakistan Defence Officers' Housing Authority and others v. Lt. Col. Syed Jawaid Ahmed (2013 SCMR 1707), which reads:

"Violation of Service Rules or Regulations framed by the Statutory bodies under the powers derived from Statutes in absence of any adequate or efficacious remedy can be enforced through writ jurisdiction."

The principle of master and servant under paragraph 50(ii) applies only where the conditions of service are governed by instructions issued for internal use. That is not the case here. CDA is a body corporate established under the Capital Development Authority Ordinance, 1960, and this Court can direct it under Article 199(1)(a)(i) of the Constitution to do what it is required by law to do. W.P No. 3352 of 2026 4 8. The result would be no different even if the Regulations were assumed to be non-statutory. The Hon’ble Supreme Court has held in Muhammad Rafi and another v. Federation of Pakistan and others (2016 SCMR 2146), with reference to paragraph 50 of Syed Jawaid Ahmed (supra), that "an aggrieved person can invoke the constitutional jurisdiction of the High Court against a public authority if he satisfies that the act of the authority is violative of the service Regulations even if they are non-statutory". In pension matters in particular, this Court has held in Muhammad Rafiq v. Vice-Chancellor, Allama Iqbal Open University and others (2023 PLC (C.S.) 1143) that "The question of payment of pension, being related to right of life under Article 9 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, cannot be overlooked irrespective of the fact whether the service rules of an autonomous body are statutory or not". The same view was taken in Zafar Ullah Khan and others v. Federation of Pakistan and others (2025 PLC (C.S.) 1462) and in Nasir Kamal (supra). The Hon’ble Supreme Court in Muhammad Yousaf v. Province of Sindh and others (2024 SCMR 1689) also observed that "The payment of pensionary benefits are protected under the law, rules and regulations even in the private sector" and that, where pension is payable, "it is a vested right and not charity". I am conscious that the rule of master and servant, as reaffirmed in General Manager, Punjab Provincial Cooperative Bank Ltd. and others v. Ghulam Mustafa and others (2024 SCMR 1458), still governs ordinary service disputes under non-statutory rules. This is not such a dispute. The petitioner's entitlement is not in issue; it stands sanctioned by CDA itself. Nothing turns on disputed facts or on the construction of a contractual term. The grievance is that a public authority has held back an admitted pension without any order and without the backing of any rule.

9. There is no adequate alternative remedy either. CDA has not shown that its grievance committee is a forum created by law or that it can direct the issuance of a pension payment order. The appeal under regulation 20.03(1)(c) lies against an order which withholds or reduces pension. Here, there is no order. The pension stands sanctioned, and CDA has neither paid it nor refused it. A retired employee cannot be expected to appeal against silence.

W.P No. 3352 of 2026 5 10. The objection based on the doctrine of election is also misconceived. The doctrine bars a party who has chosen and pursued one of several available remedies from seeking the same relief on the same facts before another forum. As explained in Trading Corporation of Pakistan v. Devan Sugar Mills Limited and others (PLD 2018 SC 828), "as long as a party does not avail of the remedy before a Court of competent jurisdiction all such remedies remain open to be invoked". The Wafaqi Mohtasib proceeded under Article 33 of the Order of 1983, which provides for informal resolution of disputes, and did not decide the complaint. Relying on CDA's letter that the case was pending in its HRD and Law Wings, the Advisor observed that the petitioner "has not yet been refused of his pensionary benefits", and advised him "to wait for the decision of the Agency and then if he is aggrieved, he may move the appropriate forum for redressal of his grievance". The petitioner has waited another six months and nothing has been decided. A forum which declined to decide the grievance cannot be treated as a remedy elected and exhausted.

11. The petition is also not hit by laches. Pension is payable month by month, and its non-payment is a continuing wrong. In Muhammad Usman v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Finance (2026 SCMR 429), the august Supreme Court held that "Neither the principle of laches would apply here (as indeed no one else has any claim over the money) nor any provision of the Limitation Act would come as an obstacle to decline the claim of pensionary benefits". This Court took the same view of a continuing wrong in Muhammad Azram (supra), and the Hon’ble Supreme Court treated an employee’s claim to advance increments as a continuing claim in Baqa Muhammad Lashari (supra). The petition is, therefore, maintainable.

12. On merits, none of the three reasons given by CDA for holding back the pension has any basis in the Regulations. The pension has been sanctioned by the competent authority, and CDA is bound to pay it. In Government of N.W.F.P. v. Muhammad Said Khan and another (PLD 1973 SC 514), the Hon’ble Supreme Court held that pension "is no longer a bounty but is a right acquired after putting in satisfactory service for the prescribed minimum period. A fortiori, it cannot be reduced or refused arbitrarily except to the extent and in the manner provided in W.P No. 3352 of 2026 6 the relevant rules". The petitioner's pension can, therefore, be refused or withheld only to the extent and in the manner provided in the Regulations.

13. The first reason, that the petitioner has less than twenty-five years of service, proceeds on a misreading of the Regulations. Regulation 19.02-A empowers the competent authority to retire an employee in the public interest after twenty-five years of qualifying service, and regulation 21.22 provides a retiring pension to an employee who chooses to retire after twenty-five years. Neither applies to the petitioner. He retired on attaining the age of sixty years. His case falls under regulation 21.21, which provides that "A superannuation pension is granted to an employee entitled or compelled by these regulations to retire at a particular age". Under regulation 21.25(1)(b), such pension is admissible "After a qualifying service of ten years or more", with a proportionate reduction where the service is less than thirty years. The petitioner has more than sixteen years of qualifying service, and the Pension Sanctioning Authority calculated his pension on that basis.

14. The second reason, of double pension, is equally without substance. Regulation 21.02 provides that "An employee cannot earn two pensions in the same post at the same time or by or for the same continuous service". The bar is against two pensions for the same service. The petitioner disclosed in his pension application that he draws a pension from PTCL for his service there up to 2007. The pension now claimed is for a different service, rendered to a different employer, from 2008 to 2024. The Regulations deal separately with earlier service. Under the proviso to regulation 21.04, service in another Government organisation counts towards pension in CDA only if the employee "has not drawn any pensionary or retirement benefits for that service". The only consequence of the PTCL benefits is, therefore, that the petitioner's PTCL service cannot be added to his CDA service. That has already been done, as his qualifying service has been reckoned from his first entry into CDA. No provision of the Regulations takes away the pension earned in CDA itself.

W.P No. 3352 of 2026 7 15. Article 529 of the Civil Service Regulations does not help CDA. It deals with an officer who, "having been discharged with a pension, is subsequently reemployed", and requires the old and new service to be counted as one. The petitioner was not re-employed; he was selected by initial appointment against a regular and pensionable post. In any case, under regulation 3.03(2) the rules of the Federal Government apply to CDA employees only "in all matters not expressly provided for in these regulations" and when "made applicable to the employee by orders of the Authority". Pension is fully provided for in Chapter 21 of the Regulations, and no order adopting Article 529 has been produced. As held in Muhammad Usman (supra), a provision meant for reckoning service cannot be used "as an independent application to oust a civil servant from a contest to claim pensionary benefits".

16. There was also nothing to verify from PTCL. The sanction itself records the petitioner's earlier service as "PTCL (Golden Hand Shake)", and the Pension Sanctioning Authority accorded sanction with that fact before it. It was not open to the Accounts Directorate to reopen the entitlement afterwards. In Muhammad Said Khan (supra), the Hon’ble Supreme Court noted that the power to reduce pension for unsatisfactory service "is however exercisable only before pension is actually sanctioned".

17. The third reason is the pendency of FIA inquiries. Under regulation 21.40(1), the Chairman may withhold or withdraw a pension "if the pensioner be convicted of serious crime or be guilty of grave misconduct", and only after giving him an opportunity to explain under regulation 21.40(4). Regulation 21.41 permits recovery from pension of a loss found in judicial or departmental proceedings, subject to time limits for proceedings instituted after retirement. None of these conditions is met. The petitioner has not been convicted. CDA does not claim that any departmental proceedings were instituted against him, and the sanction certifies that no inquiry is pending. No order has been passed under regulation 21.40. CDA has not even placed the FIR on record. All that is on record is a letter of June 2025 by which CDA itself asked FIA about the status of an FIR of 2023 and an inquiry of 2024, so as to "finalize his pension case".

W.P No. 3352 of 2026 8 18. A pension cannot be suspended in anticipation of the outcome of an inquiry. In Muhammad Said Khan (supra), while upholding the Government's power to inquire into the conduct of a retired officer under a rule similar to regulation 21.40, the Hon’ble Supreme Court held:

"... except as a result of the enquiry contemplated under clause (a), the Government has no power under the Rules to suspend the payment of whole or any part of the pension otherwise admissible to respondent No. 1 pending an enquiry against him. Therefore, any order in that behalf in anticipation of the result of the enquiry will be without any valid basis." In Nasir Kamal (supra), the High Court of Sindh held that FIA "had no jurisdiction or authority" to direct a statutory corporation to hold back the post-retirement benefits of its employee, and directed their payment. Here there is not even a direction of FIA, and the principle in Muhammad Said Khan (supra) applies whatever the outcome of the FIR may be. This does not leave CDA without a remedy. If the petitioner is ever convicted of a serious crime, or found guilty of grave misconduct, the Chairman may act under regulation 21.40. If a loss is established against him in judicial or departmental proceedings, it may be recovered under regulation 21.41. Any other dues may be recovered from the pension under regulation 21.37(6) within one year of the issue of the pension payment order. Each of these powers must, of course, be exercised strictly in accordance with the conditions laid down in the Regulations. A sanctioned pension cannot, however, be held in suspense in the meantime.

19. The Regulations also leave no room for the delay that has occurred. Under regulation 21.39(1), pension "is payable from the date on which the pensioner ceases to be borne on establishment". Under regulations 21.01(4) and 21.48, anticipatory pension was to be paid if the final pension could not be settled in time. CDA did none of this. The petitioner has not received any pension for more than two and a half years after his retirement. The Hon’ble Supreme Court in Haji Muhammad Ismail Memon (supra) directed that all departments and agencies "shall not cause unnecessary hurdle or delay in finalizing the payment of pensionary / retirement benefits cases in future and violation of these directions W.P No. 3352 of 2026 9 criminal negligence and dereliction of the duty assigned to them". The conduct of CDA falls squarely within these observations.

20. The objection of suppression of facts is without force, as the petitioner's PTCL service and benefits were disclosed by him in his pension application and are recorded in the sanction. In view of the above findings, it is not necessary to decide the plea of discrimination. The prayer for mark-up is declined, as the Regulations make no provision for it and no material has been placed on record to determine it.

21. For the foregoing reasons, this petition is allowed. The inaction of CDA in issuing the pension payment order of the petitioner and in paying his pension and commuted value is declared to be without lawful authority. CDA is directed to issue the pension payment order of the petitioner in terms of the sanction already accorded. It shall pay him the arrears of pension with effect from 01.04.2024, along with all increases admissible from time to time. It shall also pay him the commuted value of pension. All these payments shall be made within thirty days from the receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(AYYAZ SHAUKAT)
JUDGE Announced in open court on 23.11.2026.
Approved for reporting JUDGE Saeed.
